findings.title: Blocked-email matching is case-sensitive
findings.body: This exact equality lookup misses a blocked address when the signup uses different casing, especially in the domain, which is case-insensitive. Signup assigns the submitted email without normalizing it, so an address on the blocklist can register by changing its capitalization. The unique index on `email` also permits differently cased duplicate entries.

findings.title: Non-blocking matches are counted twice per signup
findings.body: `should_block?` increments `match_count`, but this validator runs as part of validation and therefore has a write side effect. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then, when validation passes, `user.save`, which validates again. For a matching `:do_nothing` entry, a single signup consequently increments `match_count` twice, so it does not represent the number of signup attempts.

findings.title: Concurrent matches can lose counter increments
findings.body: The counter update is a read-modify-save sequence. If two validations load the same `match_count` concurrently, both can save the same incremented value, losing one match. Since this field is intended to track matching attempts, use an atomic database increment or otherwise serialize updates.
